title: Privileged Access Response Kit — SSO & RBAC v2 on-call macros and runbook
creator: Maya Chen
summary: Consolidate a compact, safety-first kit for triaging and remediating privileged-access incidents across RBAC v2, SSO/SAML sessions, and audit trails. Deliver support-tool macros, vetted read-only checks, and guarded remediation steps that require approvals.
background: Post RBAC v2 rollout, on-call and support frequently need a narrow set of safe commands and queries to validate claims (e.g., "I lost access" or "I see a role change"). Existing runbooks are fragmented across Confluence pages and chat snippets. This ticket produces a single, security-reviewed artifact and an importable macro bundle for the Support tooling.
scope: Produce an authoritative JSON artifact and Confluence page containing: one-line support macros (read-only first), guarded write macros that require approvals, audit query snippets for Datadog/Kibana/warehouse, an on-call one-pager, and an escalation matrix. Include examples and explicit approval gates.
out_of_scope: Automating role schema changes, changing RBAC policy rules, building new IdP integrations, or making permanent changes to the policy engine. No backend code changes are included.
success_criteria: Support can triage >=90% of privileged-access incidents with the kit without immediate engineering intervention
Two security reviewers sign off on macros and runbook language
Support macros successfully imported into staging support tool and used in at least one drill
deliverables: support-macros.json — importable macro set for Support tooling (staging verified)
on-call one-pager PDF with escalation matrix and approval cadence
runbook_steps: Step 1 — Intake: Collect reporter email, session ID (if available), timestamp, and brief description. Create incident in #inc-rbac with collected metadata.
Step 2 — Read-only SSO checks: Run SSO-ASSERT-TRACE macro to fetch the last 10 assertions for the reporter. Confirm subject, issuer, issue timestamp, and audience. Do not perform any writes.
Step 3 — Read-only RBAC audit check: Run RBAC-AUDIT-RECENT macro to list role.grant and role.revoke events for the subject in the last 24 hours. Snapshot results for evidence.
Step 4 — Session enumeration: Use SESSION-LIST-READONLY macro to list active sessions. If a suspicious session is identified, do NOT invalidate without approval. Collect session IDs for escalation.

Step 5 — Guarded remediation (requires approval): If immediate risk (active exfiltration) is confirmed, follow TEMP-BLOCKLIST flow: create a time-limited blocklist entry (TTL) and notify Security Lead. All blocklist writes must be logged and approved in the incident channel.
Step 6 — Post-remediation: Export audit query results, mark incident for post-mortem, and schedule role review with Role Owner. Update Confluence with lessons and any new macros.
Approval note: Any macro that performs a write must be executed only after explicit approval by Security Lead or Engineering Owner (DM and two-confirmation pattern).
support_macros: SSO-ASSERT-TRACE: curl -s "$CONSOLE_URL/api/admin/sso/assertions?email={{email}}&limit=10" -H "Authorization: Bearer $READONLY_AUDIT_TOKEN" | jq '.'  # read-only; shows last assertions with timestamps

RBAC-AUDIT-RECENT: curl -s "$CONSOLE_URL/api/audit/events?subject={{email}}&types=role.grant,role.revoke&since=24h" -H "Authorization: Bearer $READONLY_AUDIT_TOKEN" | jq '.items[] | {timestamp: .timestamp, actor: .actor, action: .type, details: .details}'  # read-only
SESSION-LIST-READONLY: curl -s "$CONSOLE_URL/api/sessions?email={{email}}&status=active" -H "Authorization: Bearer $READONLY_AUDIT_TOKEN" | jq '.sessions'  # list active sessions (read-only)

TEMP-BLOCKLIST-CREATE (guarded): echo '{"target": "user:{{email}}", "reason": "emergency_privilege_block", "ttl_minutes": 60}' > payload.json && curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_APPROVAL_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" $CONSOLE_URL/api/ops/blocklist -d @payload.json  # requires in-tool approval and Security Lead confirmation

SESSION-INVALIDATE-TARGETED (guarded): curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_APPROVAL_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" $CONSOLE_URL/api/sessions/invalidate -d '{"session_ids": ["{{session_id}}"]}'  # requires approval; prefer targeted invalidation
audit_queries: Kibana/KQL: event.dataset:rbac AND user.email:"{{email}}" AND (event.action:"role.grant" OR event.action:"role.revoke")
Warehouse SQL: SELECT timestamp, actor_email, action, role_id, metadata FROM rbac_audit WHERE subject_email='{{email}}' AND timestamp > now() - interval '24 hours' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 200
troubleshooting_checklist: If SSO assertions are missing: confirm IdP delivery (IdP logs) and check for recent IdP errors or certificate rotations.
If RBAC audit shows unexpected grant: preserve evidence (export query results) and DO NOT revoke until Security Lead approves unless active compromise is clear.
If sessions cannot be enumerated: ensure audit-read tokens are valid and the audit service is healthy. Escalate to Observability if necessary.
When invalidating sessions: prefer invalidating specific session IDs; avoid global session flush unless incident dictates and approvals obtained.
escalation_matrix: Tier 1 Support: Execute read-only checks, gather evidence, and open incident in #inc-rbac. Use macros in read-only mode first.
Tier 2 / Security Oncall: Required if evidence of compromise or authorization bypass. Security Oncall must approve any write macro. Pager: Security Oncall rotation.
Engineering Owner: RBAC Runtime (Priya Nambiar) — required for DB rollbacks, policy-engine changes, or migrations.
Legal & Compliance: Consult when incident potentially affects customer data or triggers notification obligations.
